To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) event based approach for load disaggregation is effective, (ii) the use of graph signal processing techniques in the event detection and clustering stage is useful for the identification of load patterns, and (iii) the use of GSP in the load classification stage is useful for load disaggregation.

we propose a three-staged approach for electrical load disaggregation, comprising of (i). Event Detection and Clusterng (ii) Event pairing and feature extraction, and (iii) load classification, each of which are pivoted on Graph Signal Processing.
the proposed approach is capable of classifying the loads with a high accuracy and the performance of the proposed approach is superior to the state-of-the-art approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (i) A new framework for load disaggregation using event and feature based graph signal processing (ii) A novel approach to feature extraction using graph Fourier transform (iii) A new method for load classification using joint spectral clustering of graph signals (iv) A new approach to load classification using graph signals and graph Fourier transform (v) An effective method for load classification in presence of noise and missing values

the following contributions: (a) A novel approach to electrical load disaggregation is proposed, which combines the techniques of event detection and clustering with feature extraction and load classification using GSP.
